headline: High: Cline’s workspace/MCP write access plus Authelia’s broad egress creates default-path data leakage and cascading-action risk; prompt injection is lower but present via shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can expose OAuth/ForwardAuth outputs, and Cline reads workspace files plus uses MCP and browser tools, so attacker-controlled content can cross from one into the other through shared files or tool outputs. This is not proven by direct interaction evidence, but the pathway is plausible in default workspace-based use.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are copied into a shared workspace file that Cline reads
IF Cline is configured to treat file or MCP content as instructions
mitigations: Keep Authelia outputs out of shared workspace files
Use a read-only handoff file for any Authelia output
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted text
Add a prompt-injection warning banner to imported content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles authentication flows, while Cline reads and writes workspace files, captures screens, and can send content to a user-configured model provider. In a shared workspace, sensitive material can flow from Authelia into Cline and then out to third parties without a default isolation boundary.
conditions: IF Authelia artifacts containing secrets or auth tokens are placed in the shared workspace
IF Cline forwards workspace or screen content to its configured model provider
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace
Restrict Cline to a redacted subdirectory
Disable screen capture during sensitive Authelia sessions
Use a local-only model provider for Cline
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering before any outbound API call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can egress broadly, and Cline can execute shell, modify git state, write files, and use MCP in a per-workspace shared filesystem model. That overlap creates a direct write/write conflict on the same workspace and repository state, with no locking mechanism documented here.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF Cline modifies git state while Authelia-generated artifacts are also written there
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use git worktrees for isolation
Limit Cline to read-only mode for shared repos
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can produce authentication-related outputs that Cline may ingest as workspace content, and Cline can then act on them with shell, git, or MCP tools. Because Cline’s tool-use loop is autonomous and approval-based rather than verification-based, a mistaken Authelia output can cascade into downstream actions.
conditions: IF Cline treats Authelia output as authoritative input
IF that output is used to generate shell commands, commits, or MCP actions
mitigations: Require human review before any action derived from Authelia output
Add a verification step against source systems
Use structured schemas for Authelia outputs
Limit Cline to drafting only, not executing
requires-engineering: implement output validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service and Cline handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys. The pair can therefore mix operational auth data with developer artifacts, creating a compliance gap if regulated identifiers or secrets are stored in the shared workspace or sent to external providers. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated identifiers or secrets are stored in files Cline can read
IF those files are transmitted to an external model provider or retained in screenshots
mitigations: Separate regulated data from the coding workspace
Redact screenshots before review
Use a provider with an appropriate DPA
Set short retention on workspace artifacts
requires-engineering: document data-flow and residency boundaries
